source_workbook: KPI Group FY2025 GHG Emissions Summary.xlsx

notes: This spreadsheet is a broad overview of your emissions, and we ask that those involved in the data collection process undertake a general sense check of the activity data and assumptions made (total $ spent, kWh used etc.). Once the emissions summary is confirmed, Pangolin will then proceed to the remaining deliverables in the engagement.

activity_summary.activity: Overseas communication services and Pay TV
Hoists, cranes, lifting and loading machinery
Market research and other business management services

ghg_protocol_summary.description: Direct emissions from fuel combustion, chemical processing or fugitive emissions
Indirect emissions from purchased electricity, heat and steam

assumptions.assumption: Where actual data on MJ consumed could not be provided in the form of gas bills or a NABERS certificate, share of base building natural gas has been estimated according to electricity intensity metrics from 'Commercial Buildings Energy Consumption Baseline Study 2022' (Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water).
assumptions.source: Commercial Building Baseline Study 2022, Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water

assumptions.assumption:
An uplift has applied utilising the provided CEO flights to estimate the total flights of the business based on FY2024 activity data split.
An uplift has been applied to hotels stays provided as information was missing. The uplift was based on FY2024 activity data.
Data was unavailable for the NSW office, the average intensity of the iTrafic, QLD, and Vic offices has been adopted (38.47kWh/m2) and multiplied against the net occupied area of the NSW office.
Employee data was unable to be provided in FTE. Therefore, conservatively it is assumed that both part-time and casual employees are 0.6 FTE to account for the variability of the work.

A comprehensive survey of all staff was conducted in FY2025 to determine normal commuting behaviour and working from home habits. Respondents answered questions asking them to characterise a typical working week, including the days worked from home, and the mode and distance travelled when working from the office. The key survey details are:  Number of FTE = 488.8 ; Response rate = 14%; Average Emissions Intensity = 0.2 kgCO2-e/km (total emissions/total kilometres).
assumptions.source: Employee Commuting and Working From Home Survey

assumptions.assumption:
For responders that provided a qualitative answer to the percentage of time commuting in a company vehicle, the following percentage values were adopted:
- "Every working day to and from work" was changed to 100%
- "A lot" was changed to 75%

Expenditure based activities were calculated using the input/output method and may be an overestimation of actual emissions from third-party services and equipment usage. As a top-down approach, these emission factors are inherently less accurate than a process based co-efficient, however do provide for a conservative and more accessible methodology.
Hire Purchase Charge have been excluded as they are associated with internal costs for hiring vehicles
Emission factors for hotels are based on country and hotel star-rating. Where the actual star rating was unknown, an average emission factor for the country was applied.
No stationary fuels data was available, therefore FY2024 data has been adopted.

To calculate the emissions associated with refrigeration and HVAC use, global warming values from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change's (IPCC) Assessment Report 6 (AR6) have been used. These are a more up-to-date dataset of GWP's that supersede, and differ slightly from, those listed in the IPCC AR4 and A5.
assumptions.source: IPCC AR6, Supplementary Materials Chapter 7, Table 7.SM.7

assumptions.assumption: Assumed leakage rates are based on classes of unit types (depending on function and size) and the commensurate average refrigerant leakage recorded for each by the DCCEEW in the yearly National Greenhouse Accounts and in the research paper "Cold Hard Facts 4 Appendix A: Methodology – taxonomy, data and assumptions", 2024.
All synthetic GHGs were assumed to be identical to those at the same location in FY2024 and thus, the quantity per unit for NSW, and VIC has been kept the same

Consistent with FY2024, gas type and quantity per unit (kg) have been estimated for refrigerators at the ITrafic new and QLD new facilities. To be conservative the highest gas amount (0.25 kg) and gas type (R134a) has been used from a facility with actual data from FY2023.

Gas type and quantity per unit (kg) have been estimated for air conditioning appliances at the iTrafic and QLD facilities. To be conservative the highest gas amount (2 kg) and gas type (R-410A) has been used from a facility with actual data (old QLD facilities).

AdBlue has been input as part of transport fuels. AdBlue is Diesel Exhaust Fluid that is made from 32.5% high-purity urea and 67.5% deionised water (https://znz-webbackendassets-s3bucket-prod.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/public/zenergy/products-services/documents/technical-data-sheets/AdBlue-Technical-Data-Sheet.pdf). This has been modelled using a breakdown of Ecoinvent 3.10 factors: Urea {RoW}| urea production | Cut-off, U and Water, deionised {RoW}| market for water, deionised | Cut-off, U. 

A conversion factor of 1.09 kg/L has been applied, to convert the provided litres of AdBlue consumed into kgs.

Data provided indicated some consumption of "oil". This has been assumed to be diesel oil. Furthermore, the oil amounted to ~0.003% of the overall fuel consumed, and is, therefore, not material to the overall assessment.

Where actual data on tonnes of waste could not be provided, waste tonnes were estimated based on bin size, the estimated number of collections in a year, and the average fullness. This volume estimate was then converted to tonnes using the volume to weight conversion factors in table 34 in the National Greenhouse Accounts Factors (2019).
All Sanitary waste has been considered as Clinical for incineration.

By default, the cut-off method (100-0 method or recycled-content approach) has been applied to model recycling. By taking this approach, the impacts of waste management (including collection and recycling process) have been attributed to the second life cycle of the product being recycled. In line with this approach, 0 emissions have been attributed to the recycling process.
As in FY2024, no actual data on recycling was available for all sites except the iTrafic location and thus, this was excluded from the FY2024 assessment as well.

In order to calculate emissions associated with working from home, the following assumptions have been made:
• a typical working day consists of 7.6 hours
• a typical year consists of 230 working days, accounting for both federally mandated public holidays as well as an additional of 10 leave days
No responses in the survey indicated they work from home. Therefore FY2024 was adopted conservatively, noting there is a limited WFH policy
